title: Curation patch entry
description: One line of names/work/curate-patch.jsonl: a decision the curation view (web `?curate`) made about one row of names/places.csv, which `frasch curate apply` writes back. `properties` are the fields of every entry; each action has a branch of `allOf` that says which fields it needs and which others it may carry -- a field of another action is refused. The browser appends through the Vite dev server (web/vite-plugins/curate.ts), which sets `at` and stores an entry only if it keeps this schema. The rules that need the name list (is the row the matcher's, is the slug free) are apply's.

id.description: The places.csv row's `id` -- what apply finds the row by.

line.description: The row's line in places.csv when the worklist was exported; for messages only.

kind.description: The row's kind; for messages only.

name.description: The row's Frisian name; for messages only.

de.description: The row's German name; for messages only.

action.description: What is decided about the row; each action has its branch of `allOf`.

at.description: When the dev server stored the entry (ISO 8601).

then.description: The row is these OSM objects.

wikidata.description: The object's Wikidata id, if it has one.

then.description: A place OSM does not have, at lat/lon.

slug.description: The slug of the local reference `local/<slug>`.

polygon_km2.description: Label the place with a square of this area instead of a node.

then.description: The row is never on the map.
Withdraw the row's earlier decision: no field of its own.

slug.description: Lowercase ASCII letters and digits, words joined by single hyphens -- the shape of a row id and of a local reference. Both are folded from a name by one rule (`frasch.placelist.slug`): ß -> ss, æ -> ae, ø -> o, đ -> d; every other character is taken apart as Unicode's NFKD does, so a letter loses its diacritic (ä -> a, ö -> o, ü -> u, å -> a; never ae, oe, ue) and a compatibility character becomes its plain parts (ﬁ -> fi, ½ -> 12); what is still not ASCII is dropped, the rest is lowercased, every run of anything but a letter or digit becomes one hyphen, and hyphens at either end are removed: `Schörkewärw` -> `schorkewarw`, `Deezbüll Burg` -> `deezbull-burg`. A slug written by hand keeps the pattern too; a local reference may say more than the name (`westerheide-amrum`).

wikidata.description: A Wikidata id; an entry without one leaves the field out.

note.description: Free text about the decision; a `local` decision's goes into its curation row.
